[MUQATIL:69:25-32/r7] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | They are to roast him in Hell's sixth gate.
[NAHHAS:v5p21/r20] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | reports | The wāw may be retained as original; deletion is explained by the weak boundary between wāw and following hāʾ.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r10] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الكلبي | reports | Al-Kalbi glosses ṣallūhu as “put him into it.”
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p175#4/r11] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · المبرد | reports | Al-Mubarrad says both aṣlaytuhu and ṣallaytuhu mean that one sends someone into the Fire, just as one can say akramtuhu or karramtuhu.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:29-32/r3] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | “Ṣallūhu” means put him into the Fire.
[JISHUMI:v10p7063#2/r1] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Al-jaḥīm is a name for Hell and a great fire; al-jaḥīm, al-saʿīr, and al-waqūd are near-synonyms.
[JISHUMI:v10p7063#2/r2] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Taṣliya means making someone stay in the fire; its root also describes warming oneself and following a predecessor closely.
[JISHUMI:v10p7063#2/r6] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | After describing two groups through their books, the passage warns of punishment prepared for sinners.
[JISHUMI:v10p7063#2/r9] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The command is to put him into the fire and make him remain there.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r13] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Ṣallūhu means to make him enter the blazing Hell.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p608/r1] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Roast him only in the greatest Fire, fitting for a ruler who exalted himself over people.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p608/r2] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | صلى النار and صلاة النار are expressions for putting someone into the Fire.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p608/r6] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Repeated ثم marks the escalation between shackling, roasting, and threading him through the chain, not elapsed time.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p353#3/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | The command is to put him into the Fire.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p353#3/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjāj glosses it as making him enter the Fire.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r10] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The command consigns him to al-Jahim, the great fire, fitting his former arrogance as a ruler.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p101/r9] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · المبرد | reports | Al-Mubarrad says aṣlaytuhu means to expose or bring someone to the fire; ṣallaytuhu is another form, like akramtuhu and karramtuhu.
[QURTUBI-FULL:69:25-34/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Thumma al-jaḥīma ṣallūhu means make him suffer in the blazing Hellfire.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:69:30-32/r3] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | They are to roast him only in the greatest fire, fitting because he exalted himself over people.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:69:30-32/r5] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Putting the Fire and then the chain first signals particularity and draws attention to the kinds of torment; thumma marks their differing severity.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p276#7/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | “Roast him in the Inferno” means put him into the greatest Fire.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p276#7/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Alternatively, “الجحيم” is accusative under an implied verb explained by “صلوه”.
[QASHANI:69:25/r4] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | The next punishment is deprivation's inferno and suffering through an unending chain of events and varied torments.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261#2/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The command is addressed to the infernal guards: seize him, put a collar on his neck, then roast him in the great Fire.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261#2/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | He reads the fronted Fire as exclusive: they are to roast him only in the greatest Fire because he had lorded over people.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261#2/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | rejects | He rejects the exclusivity inferred from fronting as neither Sibawayh's nor expert grammarians' doctrine, and calls Ibn Zayd's kingly-status explanation weak; Ibn Abbas's proof-reading fits all the damned, not kings alone.
[SAMIN-DURR:69:30/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhsharī says fronting الجحيم restricts the destination: send him only to Hell.
[SAMIN-DURR:69:30/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشيخ | rejects | The commentator says this restriction is not the doctrine of Sībawayh or leading grammarians; the author says grammar does not rule out al-Zamakhsharī's analysis.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p215#2/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | God orders the keepers to seize him forcibly from the gathering, shackle his neck, and take him to Hell to be immersed in it.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p216/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The command means to immerse the condemned man in Hell.
[BURHAN:v1p77/r3] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | A balanced cadence can be followed by a longer second clause, as in ما ضل صاحبكم وما غوى, or by a longer third clause, as in the command to take and bind the condemned man. | mentions 69:30, 69:31
[BURHAN:v3p274#2/r1] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | The order “then the Fire, roast him” preserves the verse endings; saying “roast him in the Fire” would convey the meaning but lose their joined cadence.
[BURHAN:v3p274#2/r2] BURHAN, d. 794 · بعضهم | reports | Some also explain the unusual order as giving the Fire particular emphasis or exclusivity.
[BURHAN:v3p274#2/r4] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Verse-ending alignment can motivate multiple instances of fronting; when reasons conflict, the strongest governs, and when equal the speaker may choose either order.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p134/r6] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | “Then” marks the elevated severity of the punishment; al-jaḥīm is the immense fire that overwhelms anyone who sees it.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p134/r7] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | “Roast him” commands repeated, intense immersion in the fire, like roasting a sheep again and again.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p134/r8] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The greatest fire suits a man who tried as hard as he could to burn advisers’ hearts with his words and who exalted himself over the weak.
[BURSEVI:v10p110#2/r10] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · ابن الشيخ | reports | Ibn al-Shaykh avoids coordinating both ثم and ف on one clause by positing omitted successive commands to the wardens; ثم links the commands, while ف signals immediate execution.
[BURSEVI:v10p110#2/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Fronting al-jahim restricts the burning: admit and burn him only in the great Fire, fitting punishment for his arrogance.
[BURSEVI:v10p110#2/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · سعدى المفتي | reports | Saʿdi al-Mufti infers that the restriction applies specifically to the arrogant, because the condemned man had exalted himself over people.
[BURSEVI:v10p110#2/r9] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The repeated ثم marks increasing terror among binding, roasting, and chain punishment, not elapsed time; the scene's threat requires no pause between torments.
[ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#5/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The command means to roast him only in al-Jaḥīm, the immense, fiercely blazing fire, for his grave sin of disbelief in God.
[ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#5/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · قيل | reports | Another view says he was sent there because he exalted himself over people, taking the context as a ruler’s punishment; Al-Ālūsī answers that this may describe only one subset of left-handed people.
[ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#5/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Qatāda’s report does not rule out the ruler reading: this passage may describe some left-handed people, just as 107:3 describes a subset. | mentions 107:3
[ALUSI-FULL:v29p49#5/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · قيل | reports | Some authorities say al-Jaḥīm is the name of one particular level of Hell.
[ELMALILI:69:30-34/r2] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | These are God's commands to the keepers of Hell, phrased as an implied utterance as though addressed to the useless wealth and power mentioned by the condemned man.
[ELMALILI:69:30-34/r4] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Jahīm is a violently surging great fire, the most severe layer of Hell.
[ELMALILI:69:30-34/r5] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Putting Jahīm first restricts the destination: he is consigned to Jahīm alone, nowhere else.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p137/r11] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Fronting “Hell” and “in a chain” hastens the hearer’s distress and maintains the rhyme.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p137/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The first thumma marks a higher rank of punishment: entering the Fire is harsher than seizure and shackling.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p137/r8] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Ṣallā the Fire means to suffer its burning or warm oneself by it; when made transitive it takes the forms aṣlāhu nāran or ṣallāhu nāran.
[TABATABAI:69:27-36/r6] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | They are to put him into the tremendous Fire and make him remain bound to it.
[ASAD-NOTES:69:30/r2] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · author | holds | After shackling him, the command is to make him enter hell.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:30/r1] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | After the left-handed person's account, God orders the angels to bind his hands to his neck, take him to hell, and bind him to the criminals' long chain.
[STUDYQURAN:69:30/r1] STUDYQURAN · Q, Ṭ | reports | The commands to seize and cast the person into Hell are addressed to the angels who govern Hell.
